rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZ ING THE NATIONAL MILK FEEDING PROGRAM AND PROVIDING FOR A MILKFEEDING FUND THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Milk feeding, as used in this Act, shall cover distribution of locally produced milk from cows, carabaos and goats for direct intake of children aged 5-10 years old nationwide. The milk shall come from the produce of local dairy producers and processors at a price and quality acceptable to both the local milk suppliers and milk feeding sponsors, private or government. No milk intended for milk feeding shall be used for commercial sale. Priority shall be given to children who are in the barangayday care centers, pre-schools and schools located in the rural areas of the country and where prevalence of malnutrition is high. Second priorities are nursing mothers, pregnant women and elderly persons who also reside in rural communities.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-07-31

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO LOWER THE COSTS OF MEDICINES AND HEALTH CARE IN THE PHILIPPINES BY EXEMPTING FROM ALL DUTIES AND TAXES THE SALE, IMPORTATION, PROCESSING, REPACKING OR MANUFACTURING OF MEDICINES, PHARMACEUTICAL PRODUCTS, MEDICAL, DENTAL AND HOSPITAL EQUIPMENT, AND RAW MATERIALS TO BE USED IN THE MANUFACTURE THEREOF
rows.abstract: All transactions involving the importation, sale, manufacturing, repacking or processing of the following shall be exempt from all duties and taxes, whether covered by the National Internal Revenue Code or the Tariff and Customs Code, or otherwise:(a) medicines; (b) pharmaceutical products; (c) medical, dental and hospital equipment; (d) chemicals or preparations for the formulation of medicines; (e) raw materials to be used in the manufacture of medicines, medical products; (f) raw materialsto be used in the manufacture of medical, dental and hospital equipment; (g) processing, manufacturing or repacking of medicines, pharmaceutical products, and medical, dental and hospital equipment.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2001-07-31

rows.abstract: Rationale: The sale of prepaid cards for cellular and landline telephones in the Philippines has been largely unmonitored by the Bureau of Internal Revenue. These can conveniently be bought fromm any business establishment without the benefit of records and/or receipts. These transactions, therefore, escape the imposition and payment of the proper taxes thus depriving the government of much needed revenue.

Youth information and counseling work play a vital role inhelping young people faceup to a wide range of problems which may confront them in their daily lives. rows.abstract: "Omnibus Amendments to RA 8042." Rationale: The implementation of RA 8042 for the past five years saw the urgent need for the government to review and assess the long-term implications of certain provisions of law.  In fact, the law is now the subject of several amendatory bills pending in this august chamber. Moreover, the series of consultations with the various sectors concerned has revealed other needed amendments that are not covered by these bills. rows.abstract: The bill seeks to promote the growth of chambers of commerce and industry (CCIs) nationwide. Presently, there is no chamber of commerce and industry system for all business and economic sectors. Chambers have thus uncontrollably mushroomed accross the country with overlapping and duplication of functions and services resulting in inefficiency, and inability to provide valud added services for its members, among others. For purposes of enhancing the support of functions of CCI's in national economic growth, there is felt a need to establish a set of standards for greater efficiencies and effectiveness of Philippine CCIs.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2001-07-31

rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZ ING THE BARANGAY INTEGRATED DEVELOPMENT APPROACH FOR NUTRITION IMPROVEMENT (BIDANI) OF THE RURAL POOR AS A NETWORK PROGRAM OF PARTICIPATING STATE COLLEGES AND UNIVERSITIES, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale:  It is hereby declared the policy of the State to recognize nutrition as a basic human right, just as the rights to health and to life are. Toward this end, the State shall promote vigorously the importance of nutrition as a public good and public concern that can be achieved only through multisectoral efforts and democratic process. It shall work towards the provision of the nutritional needs of the poor sector of the Filipino society who are deprived of said right. Further, the State shall give utmost support to programs and projects that are responsive to the nutritional needs of the people.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-07-31

rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A PHILIPPINE BUSINESS REGISTRY DATABANK
rows.abstract: Rationale:  At present, there is no mechanism in the Philippines for generating and maintaining a high-integrity and sustainable business database that is truly national in scope.  There are efforts to address these needs, but they are fragmented, and suffer from lack of program sustainability, formats and integrity. Thus, there is a need to establish a unified, reliable and sustainable mechanism in the form of a Philippine Business Registry Databank (PBRD).

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING CERTAIN LOCAL OFFICIALS TO FILL THE VACANCY IN THE OFFICES OF THE GOVERNOR OR MAYOR AND VICE-GOVERNOR OR VICE-MAYOR AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 44 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.title_short: Prohibiting Certain Local Officials To Fill the Vacancy in their Offices
rows.abstract: Rationale: Section 44 of the Local Government Code delineates the line succession in case of vacancy in the offices of the governor or mayor, the vice-governor or vice-mayor and the sanggunian member.  It is however, silent as to whether the official, who is next in the line of succession, can fill the very same vacant position he is prohibited by law to serve beyond three (3) consecutive term limits. This situation may sow confusion if not chaos in some areas where intense political rivalry isprevailing among opposing camps.  This bill seeks to amend the aforementioned provision in the Local Government Code to provide a crystal clear mandate on succession.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2002-05-23, transmitted to on 2002-05-28 and received by the Senate on 2002-05-28

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING GREATER PROTECTION TO LOCAL INDUSTRIES THROUGH THE IMPOSITION OF ANTI-DUMPING DUTY, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 301, PART 2, TITLE II, BOOK I OF THE TARIFF AND CUSTOMS CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8752
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to address the many weaknesses found in the Anti-Dumping Law Act of 1999 (Republic Act 8752) viewed by certain quaters of industry to only work to the detriment of local producers.  It restores the method/steps necessary to determinethe normal value of the article/s subject of a dumping protest which was removed when R.A. 8752 superseded RA 7843 (Anti-Dumping Law of 1994). The bill removes the posting of a surety bond by an affected industry or interested party when it files a complaint or petition against dumping.  It deletes the provision in the Tariff and Customs Code of the Philippines which allows the Tariff Commission to decide whether or not to impose a definitive anti-dumping duty.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ENTITLING THE CHILDREN OF TEACHERS AND EMPLOYEES EMPLOYED IN PUBLIC AND PRIVATE INSTITUTIONS OF HIGHER EDUCATION TO FREE TUITION AND OTHER FEES
rows.abstract: Rationale:  It is declared the policy of the State to provide other economic benefits to teachers and employees of public and private schools, colleges, universities and post-secondary vocational and technical institutions by extending to their children free tuition and fees in the educational institution where either or both of them are employed. This new benefit shall form part of the economic package already being received by the teachers and the employees on account of their employment withthese institutions. This policy is more in keeping with the commitment to help alleviate the difficulties encountered by said teachers and employees in sending their children to these institutions because of the prohibitive cost of college educationn nowadays.
